title: The One Habit Slowly Destroying Your Thinking
description:
Have you noticed something strange?

We can binge-watch three-hour podcasts, scroll endlessly through social media, and listen to hours of voice notes. But ask us to write a single thoughtful page, and suddenly it feels like hard work.

This video isn't really about writing. It's about something much bigger.

Writing is one of the most powerful thinking tools humans have ever invented. It forces us to organize ideas, challenge our own beliefs, and discover what we actually know. As we slowly replace writing with voice notes, AI, and passive consumption, we may be losing something far more valuable than neat handwriting.

We may be losing the ability to think deeply.

In this video, we'll explore why writing feels so difficult, why children naturally resist it, how it shaped science and civilization, and why its disappearance should concern all of us.

comments.text:
Just today, I experienced a "whoaa" moment, and it made me feel (again) why AI would dull our cognitive abilities.

From some random train of thought, I just wondered why all angles in a triangle should add up to only 180 degrees. I'm not from mathematical background, I have no touch with maths except school level maths which I'm sure I largely forgot. And I dont remember ever thinking of that question in the school. For a second, I had the temptation to look for AI answer, but I thought about it for a minute and the solution just occured to me. If 2 of 3 angles were to be zero degree, then all vertices will be in a straight line, so 3rd angle would be forced to be 180° at maximum. So it would be same with parallelogram  (chose this because in rectangle, by defintion, all angles should be 90°), pentagon and hexagon, if any 2 angles were to be zero degree, then all other angles would be forced to be 180° at maximum, hence it would be 360° for parallelogram, 540° for Pentagon, and 720° for Hexagon. 

Turns out I'm correct about all of them, but if I had used AI, it would have stolen my oppurtunity to solve the problem in a special "what if" method. Now after searching for AI answer, it didn't mention my way of approach, it gave another approach. If an amateur in maths like me could think of it, then many others also could, but immediately searching for an AI answer might just hinder that.
